projectRules.text: Use simple business words and Title Case labels that non-native English speakers understand.
Date format, time zone, currency, decimals and separators come from general_settings; never hardcode currency text or formats.
inventory_stock_movements is the stock history source of truth; inventory_stock_balances is only a snapshot.
Do not hardcode database users, hosts, company IDs, currency symbols, fiscal years or account ranges in feature code.
Draft documents have no ledger or stock effect; posted documents are immutable and corrected only by reversal, return or adjustment.
Posting follows ACCOUNTING_POSTING_RULES.md; GL inventory and stock valuation must agree.
vouchers.total_debit and total_credit store the sum of voucher lines and must always be equal.
Cash Book, Bank Book, Customer Ledger and Supplier Ledger are required books.
Schema changes and seeds belong in backend Prisma migrations.
Use backend .env values for configuration; no environment-specific values in code.
Users work in one Branch or one Warehouse; Admin and Top Management see all branches.
Access must be enforced in the backend with resolveAccessScope.
Every screen follows DESIGN.md (Calm Ledger) and the modular page-as-orchestrator pattern; no large single-file screens.
Required fields show *; amounts right-aligned; voucher forms keep actions on top with consistent line-item and summary areas.
Show features only when the backend and database save and validate them; no user action fails silently.

strengths.title: Every API route now requires sign-in; tokens are re-checked against the database each request, and client-supplied company IDs are verified (403 otherwise)
Salted scrypt password hashing with constant-time compare and timing-safe unknown-user handling
Branch / Warehouse scoping enforced in the backend on lists, details and posting
Single stock holder enforced in the database (CHECK + NULLS NOT DISTINCT unique)
Each document post is one locked transaction (FOR UPDATE + Draft check) — no double posting; negative stock checked against locked balance
decimal.js with explicit HALF_UP rounding for money (2dp) and quantity (4dp) in document posting; reports sum in SQL/Decimal on Posted vouchers only
Complete Calm Ledger token system with light/dark parity, global focus ring, reduced-motion support, accessible SearchableSelect and focus-trapping ConfirmDialog
Startup env validation, liveness + database readiness endpoints, safe env-driven admin seed, non-root containers

executive.summary: Since the 17 Oct audit the team closed the biggest exposure (the API now requires sign-in, company access is verified, mock logins are gone, containers run as non-root, CVE versions are patched). Stock quantities and branch/warehouse access are now well protected. However, the general ledger and financial statements cannot yet be trusted: posted vouchers can be voided without reversal, the Balance Sheet stops balancing after the first year-end, and three costing paths make GL inventory drift from stock value. Operations cannot apply migrations or restore from backup. Recommended path: a 2-week stabilisation sprint (Wave 0 + core Wave 1), then a parallel run against the current books for one month-end close before go-live.

personas.text: Calculation core is sound — posted-only filtering, Decimal sums, opening/period/closing Trial Balance, imbalance warnings. But opening balances vanish mid-year (DATA-014), year close posts no retained-earnings entry (DATA-002), opening balances are freely editable (DATA-015), and the COA balance disagrees with reports (DATA-016). Required books (Cash/Bank Book, Customer/Supplier Ledger, aging, tax) are missing and nothing can be printed or exported.

Good architecture choices: one locked transaction per document post, DB-enforced single stock holder, Decimal with HALF_UP rounding, snapshot of account code/name on GL lines. Integrity gaps: void-without-reversal (DATA-001), purchase discount and COGS timing break GL↔stock reconciliation (DATA-003/004), adjustment posting rewrites the chart of accounts (DATA-005), no Dr=Cr assertion on document posting (DATA-006), no role-based permissions or maker-checker (AUTH-001/002).

The production image cannot run migrations (OPS-001); 500 errors are not logged (OPS-002); no backup, restore or rollback (OPS-006); HTTP only (SEC-012); live secrets remain in git history (SEC-001); and the auth system, migrations, tests and CI are uncommitted (QUAL-004). Positives: startup env validation, health and DB-readiness endpoints, a safe admin seed, non-root containers.

Master-data and stock screens (Branches, Areas, Products, Transfers) look calm and professional. The daily document screens (Purchase, Sale, Journal) feel like a different, denser app, can clip fields at 1280px, and have no keyboard line entry or shortcuts. Approve posts without confirmation, and some errors look like empty lists.

findings.description: Real production database password and the shared JWT/NextAuth secret remain recoverable from git history (commit f58a6b1 added deployment/.env.backend and .env.frontend with live values). The working tree now uses placeholders and the files are git-ignored, but history was never purged. The untracked root REMEDIATION_PLAN.md also repeats the old DB password and the 64-char secret in plain text. Frontend and backend share the same secret, and the DB host is a public IP.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the DB password and both secrets now (use different values for JWT and NextAuth). Purge the files from history with git filter-repo before any push, redact the root REMEDIATION_PLAN.md, and restrict PostgreSQL port 5432 on the server to the application host only.
findings.fixPrompt: Redact every plaintext password and secret from REMEDIATION_PLAN.md (replace with ****). Do not print the values. Then list the exact git filter-repo command needed to remove deployment/.env.backend and deployment/.env.frontend from all history, but do not run it.

findings.description: Any posted voucher can be voided in place: void() checks only that the status is not already Voided. There is no voucher-type guard, no open-period/locked-year check, no role check and no reversal entry. Reports read only status='Posted', so voiding a sale/purchase/return/adjustment voucher silently removes it from the GL while the source document stays Posted and its stock movements remain. Closed-year figures can be rewritten. Sales, purchases and returns have no reversal flow at all.
findings.evidence:
if (voucher.status === 'Voided') throw businessError(...);
const updated = await prisma.voucher.update({ where: { id }, data: { status: 'Voided', ... } });
findings.recommendation: Allow Void only for Draft vouchers. For Posted vouchers add a Reverse action that posts a mirror voucher dated in an open period and links both. Block void/reverse of source-generated voucher types (SI, PI, SR, PR, SA, ST) from the voucher screen; those must be reversed from their source document.
findings.fixPrompt: In backend/src/modules/vouchers/voucher.service.ts change void() to reject any voucher whose status is not Draft. Add a reverse(id, reason, userId) method that, inside one prisma.$transaction, locks the voucher row, asserts it is Posted and is a manual voucher type, asserts the reversal date is in an open period using the shared posting-date helper, creates a new Posted voucher with debit and credit swapped on every line, and records reversed_by_voucher_id / reversal_of_voucher_id. Expose POST /vouchers/:id/reverse. Add tests.

findings.description: Closing a fiscal year only updates status and lock fields; no closing entry moves Income/Expense balances to Retained Earnings. The Balance Sheet computes profit only from the current fiscal-year start, so from the second year on Assets ≠ Liabilities + Equity by the total of all prior years' profit. Nothing in the codebase references retained earnings.
findings.evidence:
await tx.fiscalPeriod.updateMany({ ... data: { status: 'closed' } });
await tx.fiscalYear.update({ ... data: { status: 'closed', closingCompletedAt: new Date() } });
findings.recommendation: Add a Retained Earnings account to posting-account settings. On year close, post an immutable Closing voucher that zeroes every Income and Expense account into Retained Earnings. Until then, the Balance Sheet must show 'Retained Earnings (Prior Years)' = cumulative profit before the current fiscal-year start.
findings.fixPrompt: Add retainedEarningsAccountId to posting account settings (Prisma migration + settings UI field). In fiscal-year.service.ts close(), inside the existing transaction, compute each Income and Expense account balance for the year in Decimal, post one Closing voucher (type CL) dated the year end that clears them into Retained Earnings, and store closing_voucher_id on the fiscal year. In balance-sheet-report.service.ts add prior-years retained earnings. Add an integration test: two years of activity, close year 1, Balance Sheet for year 2 has difference 0.

findings.description: Purchase posting debits Inventory at gross amount (before discount) while the stock movement is valued net of line discount, so every discounted purchase leaves GL Inventory permanently higher than stock value. Same pattern in purchase returns. Under IAS 2 trade discounts reduce inventory cost. The conflict originates in ACCOUNTING_POSTING_RULES.md.
findings.evidence:
const inventoryAmount = this.money(invoice.gross_amount);          // GL
const lineCost = ...times(line.purchase_price).minus(line.discount_amount); // stock
findings.recommendation: Debit Inventory at the sum of net line costs (the same value written to stock movements). Treat freight/other charges consistently (capitalise into cost or expense, but the same way in both GL and stock). Update ACCOUNTING_POSTING_RULES.md.
findings.fixPrompt: In purchase-post.service.ts and purchase-return-post.service.ts compute the Inventory GL amount as the sum of the exact per-line costs written to inventory_stock_movements and remove the separate purchase-discount income line for line discounts. Update documents/ACCOUNTING_POSTING_RULES.md. Add a test asserting GL inventory debit equals sum of movement values for a discounted purchase.

findings.description: Sale cost of goods sold is frozen at the weighted-average cost when the draft was saved, not at posting. On posting, stock value is floored at zero (Decimal.max(0, ...)) while GL Inventory is credited with the full cost, so stock value and GL diverge. Header cost is rounded once over the total while lines are rounded individually (cent drift). Same zero floor in purchase returns and stock adjustments; sale returns are costed at current average, not original sale cost.
findings.evidence:
newValue = Decimal.max(0, oldValue.minus(lineCost))   // stock
// GL credit Inventory = invoice.cost_amount (from draft time)
findings.recommendation: Compute each line's cost from the locked balance row at post time; set header cost and the GL COGS/Inventory amounts to the sum of line costs; replace the zero floor with an error; cost sale returns at the original sale line's cost when linked.
findings.fixPrompt: In sale-post.service.ts, inside the posting transaction after locking each balance row (sorted by item id), compute line cost = quantity × current average cost (Decimal, HALF_UP 2dp), update the sale line cost_amount, sum them for the header and use that sum for the COGS debit and Inventory credit. Replace Decimal.max(0, ...) with a thrown business error in sale, purchase-return and stock-adjustment posting. Add a test that interleaves a purchase between sale draft and post.

findings.description: Every stock-adjustment post upserts three hardcoded GL accounts (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET name, account_type, is_deleted=false) and overwrites default_inventory_account_id and the adjustment accounts in posting settings. User-configured accounts are reset on every post; renamed or deleted accounts are silently restored. Hardcoded account codes break project rules.
findings.evidence:
code: '0101300301', ...
ON CONFLICT (company_id, code) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, ... is_deleted = false
ON CONFLICT (company_id) DO UPDATE SET default_inventory_account_id = EXCLUDED...
findings.recommendation: Remove the upserts from the posting path. Seed default adjustment accounts once (seed/onboarding) and read them from posting-account settings; fail with a clear message if not configured.
findings.fixPrompt: In stock-adjustment.service.ts delete the ensure-accounts/upsert logic called during posting. Read inventory, adjustment-gain and adjustment-loss account ids from posting account settings (as sale-support.service.ts does) and throw a business error 'Stock adjustment accounts are not set in Posting Account Settings' when missing. Move default account creation into the seed.

findings.description: Account opening balance is dropped entirely from Trial Balance and Ledger when its opening-balance date falls after the report Date From. Default Date From is 1 January, so a mid-year go-live date makes opening balances vanish from both the opening and closing columns.
findings.recommendation: Include the opening balance when its date ≤ Date To: in the Opening column when before Date From, otherwise as a period movement line dated on the opening-balance date.
findings.fixPrompt: In trial-balance-report.service.ts and ledger-report.service.ts change the opening-balance inclusion rule: if openingBalanceDate <= dateFrom (or null) add to opening; else if openingBalanceDate <= dateTo add it to period debit/credit (by normal balance side) and, in the ledger, as a dated 'Opening Balance' row. Add tests for both cases.

findings.description: The production image cannot apply database migrations: the runner stage installs with --omit=dev (drops the prisma CLI and tsx) and starts node dist/server.js; deploy.sh refers to 'db push' and a pgvector step and never runs prisma migrate deploy. The 20 migrations — including the two new users/access and branch-stock migrations — and seed:admin cannot be run on the server.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-off migrate service/job (image with prisma CLI) that runs `prisma migrate deploy` before the API starts, plus a compiled seed:admin step. Remove the pgvector/db push steps from deploy.sh.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a 'migrate' stage to backend/Dockerfile that keeps the prisma CLI and runs `npx prisma migrate deploy`. In deployment/docker-compose.yml add a migrate service that the backend depends_on with condition service_completed_successfully. Compile prisma/seed-admin.ts in the build and document `docker compose run --rm migrate node dist/prisma/seed-admin.js`. Remove db push/pgvector lines from deploy.sh.

findings.description: No role-based permission checks on financial actions. The only backend role check is requireUserManager. Any signed-in user (including Viewer or Sales Staff) can approve, post and void vouchers, close/lock/unlock fiscal years and periods, and change company, general and posting-account settings, branches, warehouses, accounts and bank accounts.
findings.evidence: export function requireUserManager(...)   // the only role gate in the backend
findings.recommendation: Add requirePermission(action) with a role×action matrix (e.g. post/approve: Accountant, Manager+; fiscal close/unlock and settings: Admin, Top Management) and apply it in every state-changing route. Hide matching UI actions from roles that lack them.
findings.fixPrompt: Create backend/src/http/permissions.ts with a Permission enum (VoucherApprove, VoucherPost, VoucherReverse, FiscalClose, FiscalUnlock, SettingsManage, MasterDataManage, ReportsFinancialView) and a role→permissions map. Add requirePermission(p) middleware that reads the role from the auth context and returns 403. Apply it to vouchers, fiscal-years, settings, accounts, branches, warehouses, bank-accounts and reports routes. Add tests for 403 per role.

findings.description: No maker-checker on voucher approval: approve() checks only approvalStatus === 'Pending' and never compares the approver with the creator or requester, so a user can approve their own voucher.
findings.recommendation: Reject approval when userId equals createdBy or approvalRequestedBy; require the VoucherApprove permission.
findings.fixPrompt: In voucher.service.ts approve() and reject(), throw businessError('You cannot approve a voucher you created or submitted.') when userId equals voucher.createdBy or voucher.approvalRequestedBy. Add a test.

findings.description: Users are global across companies but managed per company. Top Management in company A can change role, email, active status or reset the password of a user who also has access to company B. Promoting a user to top_management turns all their access rows in every company into ALL_BRANCHES.
findings.evidence: update/resetPassword only check that the target user has access to the actor's company
findings.recommendation: Block identity changes (role, email, active, password) for users with access to companies the actor does not manage, or move role onto user_company_access. Prevent Top Management resetting other Top Management users.
findings.fixPrompt: In user.service.ts update() and resetPassword(), load all company access rows of the target user and throw 403 if any company is outside the actor's managed companies (Admin exempt). Prevent role escalation to top_management/admin by non-admins. Add tests.

findings.description: Financial reports (Trial Balance, Ledger, P&L, Balance Sheet) use only resolveCompanyId, not resolveAccessScope, and vouchers have no branch_id. Branch and Warehouse users see company-wide financial statements, and branch-level P&L is impossible.
findings.evidence: const companyId = resolveCompanyId(req);   // no access scope
findings.recommendation: Gate financial reports behind a ReportsFinancialView permission now. Later, add branch_id to vouchers (set from the source document holder) and a Branch filter on all financial reports.
findings.fixPrompt: Apply requirePermission(ReportsFinancialView) to all routes in reports.routes.ts. Then add nullable branch_id to vouchers via migration, populate it in sale/purchase/return/adjustment posting from the document's branch, and add an optional branchId filter to the trial balance, ledger, P&L and balance sheet services.

findings.description: Sales, purchases and returns post GL vouchers without asserting Σdebit = Σcredit or header total = Σlines; the header total is computed from document fields. No database CHECK or trigger exists. A missing tax account with tax > 0 throws a plain Error (HTTP 500).
findings.recommendation: Build lines first, sum them in Decimal, assert Dr = Cr and header = Σlines before insert; add a shared assertBalancedVoucher helper and a deferred constraint trigger on voucher_lines.
findings.fixPrompt: Create backend/src/modules/vouchers/assert-balanced.ts exporting assertBalancedVoucher(lines) that sums debit and credit with decimal.js and throws businessError when unequal. Call it in every *-post.service.ts and voucher.service.ts before inserting, and set vouchers.total_debit/total_credit from the sums. Replace plain Error for missing accounts with businessError.

findings.description: Manual vouchers sum amounts with JavaScript floats and accept any precision (z.number()); balance is checked with a 0.001 tolerance, so 0.005 differences pass and un-rounded amounts are stored.
findings.recommendation: Validate amounts to 2 decimal places in the schema, sum with Decimal and require exact equality (reuse assertBalancedVoucher).
findings.fixPrompt: In voucher.schema.ts validate dr_amount/cr_amount as non-negative with at most 2 decimal places. In voucher.service.ts replace float sums with decimal.js and call assertBalancedVoucher.

findings.description: Manual voucher type 'PI' uses the same PI-YYYY-NNNN number format as purchase invoices. A manual PI takes max(posted PI)+1, which can equal an unposted draft purchase's number; posting that purchase then fails on uq_voucher_number.
findings.recommendation: Remove source-document types (PI, SI, SR, PR) from the manual voucher type list.
findings.fixPrompt: In voucher.service.ts remove 'PI' (and any other source-document prefixes) from the manual voucher types and from the frontend voucher type selector.

findings.description: The posting-period check joins on fp.end_date + posting_cutoff_days >= date and takes LIMIT 1 with no ORDER BY, so a date in a closed period can match the previous open period's cutoff window (or the reverse). The query is duplicated into every post service.
findings.recommendation: Match the period that contains the date; apply the cutoff only as an extra allowance for the immediately preceding period. Use one shared helper everywhere.
findings.fixPrompt: Rewrite posting-date.service.ts to select the period where start_date <= date <= end_date and require it open; separately allow the cutoff grace only when posting into the previous period. Replace the copied SQL in all *-post.service.ts with calls to this helper. Add tests for boundary dates.

findings.description: Sale and purchase returns are not linked to the original invoice, so a user can return more than was sold/bought to that party, at any price, without reference to the original cost.
findings.evidence: no sale_invoice_id / purchase_invoice_id column in the return migrations
findings.recommendation: Add an optional source invoice link on returns, validate remaining returnable quantity and use the original line cost.
findings.fixPrompt: Add nullable source_sale_id/source_sale_line_id to sale returns (and the purchase equivalent) via migration; when set, validate returned qty <= sold qty minus previous returns and copy the original unit cost.

findings.description: Audit-trail and concurrency gaps: manual voucher post reads then writes outside a transaction with no row lock; fiscal-year close/lock/unlock take no user id so locked_by_user_id is never set.
findings.evidence: post(): findFirst(...) then update(...) — no $transaction / FOR UPDATE
findings.recommendation: Post inside a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and a Draft-status guard; pass the acting user into fiscal-year actions and record who/when.
findings.fixPrompt: Wrap voucher.service.ts post() in prisma.$transaction, lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, re-check status. Pass req user id into fiscal-year close/lock/unlock/period-close and persist it in locked_by_user_id / closed_by fields.

findings.description: The fiscal-close 'Trial Balance Is Balanced' pre-check sums only the year's voucher lines (already balanced individually), ignores opening balances and uses Number, so it can never detect a real imbalance.
findings.recommendation: Call the real Trial Balance service (with opening balances) as of year end and compare closing debit and credit in Decimal.
findings.fixPrompt: In fiscal-year.service.ts replace the custom balance check with a call to the trial balance report service for the year range and compare totals with decimal.js .eq().

findings.description: Account opening balances can be edited at any time with no Dr = Cr check across accounts, no voucher and no lock after periods close. This directly changes historical reports.
findings.recommendation: Capture opening balances through an Opening Balance voucher (or a locked opening-balance batch) that must balance; block edits once any period is closed.
findings.fixPrompt: Add an Opening Balance entry screen and backend endpoint that posts a balanced 'OB' voucher dated the go-live date. Make account.openingBalance read-only once any period is closed and require total opening debits = credits.

findings.description: Chart of Accounts 'Current Balance' adds opening balance and movement without applying the account's debit/credit side, while reports negate credit-side opening balances. The COA screen disagrees with the Trial Balance for every liability, equity and income account with an opening balance.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the reports' signedOpeningBalance helper; move it into a shared balance module used by both.
findings.fixPrompt: Move signedOpeningBalance from trial-balance-report.service.ts into backend/src/modules/accounts/account-balance.ts and use it in account-list.service.ts current-balance calculation. Add a test that COA balance equals Trial Balance closing for a credit-nature account.

findings.description: The Bank Reconciliation tab runs on hardcoded sample data and a fixed month; 'Load Statement' only sets a message. Users would see fake reconciliation results as if real.
findings.recommendation: Hide the tab for go-live (Quick Win), then build it on a backend endpoint (statement import, match to bank-account ledger lines, reconciled flag).
findings.fixPrompt: In frontend/src/app/(dashboard)/bank/page.tsx remove the Bank Reconciliation tab and the SAMPLE_RECON data. Leave a TODO referencing a backend reconciliation endpoint.

findings.description: Required ledgers and statutory reports are missing. ACCOUNTING_POSTING_RULES.md names Cash Book, Bank Book, Customer Ledger and Supplier Ledger as required; none exist. Also missing: AR/AP aging, Day Book/Journal register, Stock Ledger and stock value as of a date, Sales Tax/VAT report, Cash Flow statement, prior-period comparatives, item-wise sales/margin.
findings.evidence: reports present: Ledger, Trial Balance, P&L, Balance Sheet, 4 document summaries, Stock Summary
findings.recommendation: Build in priority order: Customer/Supplier Ledger + AR/AP Aging, Cash Book/Bank Book, Day Book, Sales Tax report, Stock Ledger with as-of valuation, then Cash Flow and comparatives.
findings.fixPrompt: Add backend report services and routes for Customer Ledger and Supplier Ledger (reuse ledger-report on the party's linked account), AR Aging and AP Aging (buckets 0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ from posted invoices minus receipts/payments), Cash Book and Bank Book (ledger on cash/bank accounts from settings), and Day Book (all posted vouchers in a date range). Add matching pages under frontend reports.

findings.description: Stock Summary is warehouse-only, current snapshot only (no as-of date) and is never reconciled to the GL Inventory account, although /branches/:id/stock-summary exists. There is also no routine to rebuild inventory_stock_balances from inventory_stock_movements.
findings.evidence: only warehouses offered in the holder selector
findings.recommendation: Add Branch/Warehouse holder choice, an as-of date computed from stock movements, a 'Stock Value vs Inventory Account' reconciliation report, and an admin rebuild-balances job.
findings.fixPrompt: Extend stock-summary.service.ts with an asOfDate parameter that aggregates inventory_stock_movements up to that date per holder. Add a reconciliation endpoint comparing Σ total_stock_value with the GL Inventory account balance. Add Branch to the holder selector in ReportsWorkspace.tsx.

findings.description: Fallback secrets remain outside production: the backend signs tokens with a public default JWT secret whenever NODE_ENV != production; the frontend falls back to 'dev-only-secret-placeholder-for-local-testing'. A staging/demo server left on development accepts forged tokens.
findings.recommendation: Remove defaults; require secrets in every environment except test.
findings.fixPrompt: In backend/src/config/env.ts remove the JWT_SECRET default and require it unless NODE_ENV === 'test'. In frontend auth.options.ts and the api proxy route remove the fallback string and throw when NEXTAUTH_SECRET is missing.

findings.description: Login throttling is per-email, in memory and unbounded: password spraying across many emails is not limited, anyone can lock any user out for 15 minutes, the map resets on restart and is not shared across replicas, and /auth/change-password has no limit.
findings.evidence: const failedAttempts = new Map<string, ...>()   // keyed by email only
findings.recommendation: Add a per-IP limiter (express-rate-limit with trust proxy and forwarded client IP), a shared store (DB/Redis), a size cap, and limit change-password.
findings.fixPrompt: Add express-rate-limit to /auth/login and /auth/change-password keyed by client IP (set app.set('trust proxy', 1) and forward x-forwarded-for from the Next proxy). Keep the per-email lockout but cap the map size and evict expired entries.

findings.description: The deployment serves the app over plain HTTP on a public IP and issues 7-day backend tokens while the NextAuth session lasts 12 hours.
findings.recommendation: Put the app behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy/Nginx + Let's Encrypt), set secure cookies, and align JWT_EXPIRES_IN with the 12h session.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a Caddy service to deployment/docker-compose.yml terminating TLS for the frontend; bind frontend/backend ports to 127.0.0.1 only; set JWT_EXPIRES_IN=12h; set NEXTAUTH_URL to the https URL.

findings.description: Prisma schema and migrations disagree: the schema declares GL indexes that no migration creates, and the branch-stock migration creates indexes, holder CHECK constraints and NULLS NOT DISTINCT uniques that the schema does not declare. The next `prisma migrate dev` will try to reconcile both sides and may drop the branch-stock constraints.
findings.recommendation: Add a migration creating the two GL indexes, represent the raw-SQL constraints in the schema (or document them as raw migrations), and gate CI on `prisma migrate diff --exit-code`.
findings.fixPrompt: Run `npx prisma migrate diff --from-migrations prisma/migrations --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --shadow-database-url $SHADOW` and create a migration for the missing GL indexes. Add the branch-stock indexes to schema.prisma with matching map names. Add the migrate diff check to CI.

findings.description: Document-number sequencing is fixed for sales, purchases, returns and transfers, but manual vouchers still have no lock and sort numbers as text, and stock adjustments lock only the last row (the first number of a year races). Every ORDER BY *_number DESC with 4-digit padding breaks after 9999: SI-2026-9999 sorts above SI-2026-10000, so 10000 is reissued and later inserts fail the unique constraint.
findings.evidence: ORDER BY voucher_number DESC LIMIT 1   -- text sort, no lock
findings.recommendation: Use a document_sequences table (company, type, year → next_number) incremented with UPDATE ... RETURNING inside the posting transaction, for every document type.
findings.fixPrompt: Create a document_sequences table and a nextDocumentNumber(tx, companyId, type, year) helper using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET next_number = next_number + 1 RETURNING next_number. Replace every MAX/ORDER BY number lookup in vouchers, sales, purchases, returns, transfers and adjustments.

findings.description: Server errors are never logged: the error handler returns 'Unexpected server error' for 500s without logging; there are no unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers; Prisma P2002/P2025 surface as 500.
findings.evidence: res.status(500).json({ message: 'Unexpected server error' })   // nothing logged
findings.recommendation: Add a structured logger (pino), log every 5xx with request id and user/company, add process handlers, map Prisma P2002 → 409 and P2025 → 404.
findings.fixPrompt: Add pino and pino-http to the backend. Log errors in error-handler.ts with req.id, userId and companyId (no request bodies). Map Prisma P2002 to 409 and P2025 to 404. Register process.on('unhandledRejection') and ('uncaughtException') to log and exit.

findings.description: The root docker-compose.yml (the one README tells people to use) cannot start in production mode: backend has NODE_ENV=production but no JWT_SECRET so startup exits; Postgres defaults to trust auth with an empty password published on 0.0.0.0:5432; the frontend receives unused DATABASE_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL but not BACKEND_API_INTERNAL_URL, so it calls localhost:4000 inside the container.
findings.recommendation: Make the root compose explicitly dev-only (password required, scram-sha-256, bind 127.0.0.1) and point production users to deployment/.
findings.fixPrompt: Rewrite root docker-compose.yml as a development stack: require POSTGRES_PASSWORD, remove the trust default, bind 127.0.0.1:5432, set NODE_ENV=development with JWT_SECRET from .env, give the frontend BACKEND_API_INTERNAL_URL=http://backend:4000/api/v1. Update README.

findings.description: No backups, restore runbook or rollback: images default to :latest, deploy.sh runs `compose down` then `up -d` (downtime), takes no pg_dump before deploying, and there is no backup/restore document anywhere.
findings.evidence:
image: ...:${APP_TAG:-latest}
docker compose down && docker compose up -d
findings.recommendation: Use immutable version tags, run pg_dump before every migration, schedule daily encrypted off-server backups with retention, write and rehearse a restore and rollback runbook.
findings.fixPrompt: Update deploy.sh: require APP_TAG (no latest), run pg_dump -Fc to a dated file before migrate, then `docker compose up -d` without down. Add deployment/BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md with a daily cron backup, retention, off-site copy and tested restore steps, plus rollback to the previous tag.

findings.description: Release hygiene risk: 130 uncommitted changes on the feature branch; the entire auth system, users module, two migrations, seed-admin, backend tests, CI workflow and frontend middleware are untracked (no review, no CI history, one disk failure from loss). .impeccable/ review screenshots (≈229 PNG, 33 MB) are committed; audit/ (≈871 MB) is untracked and not ignored.
findings.recommendation: Commit the work in reviewed PRs (auth+users, branch stock, CI/tests), remove .impeccable/review from git, and ignore audit/results and audit/branding.
findings.fixPrompt: Split the working tree into reviewable commits: (1) auth middleware, users and access + migration 20261020100000, (2) branch stock + migration 20261020110000, (3) tests and CI. Add .impeccable/review/ and audit/results/, audit/branding/ to .gitignore and git rm --cached them.

findings.description: The GL composite indexes for reports (company+status+date, company+account+voucher) exist only in schema.prisma, not in any migration, so a database built from migrations lacks them; Trial Balance, Ledger and Balance Sheet scan voucher_lines as data grows.
findings.recommendation: Create the indexes in a migration (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY for live DBs) and verify with EXPLAIN on the report queries.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a migration that creates idx_vouchers_company_status_date_id and idx_voucher_lines_company_account_voucher matching schema.prisma. Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the trial balance query before and after.

findings.description: Stock transfer and stock adjustment list endpoints LEFT JOIN lines and GROUP BY every matching document before LIMIT (fixed for sales, purchases and returns).
findings.evidence: LEFT JOIN ..._lines l ... GROUP BY t.id ... LIMIT $n
findings.recommendation: Page the headers first, then count lines only for the page rows (as sale-list.service.ts does).
findings.fixPrompt: Rewrite the list queries in stock-transfer.service.ts and stock-adjustment.service.ts to select the page of headers in a CTE with LIMIT/OFFSET and compute line counts with a correlated subquery for those rows only, following sale-list.service.ts:145-149.

findings.description: Posting transactions for sales, purchases, returns and adjustments use Prisma's default 5-second interactive transaction timeout and insert voucher lines one at a time (~4 statements per line); large invoices will time out and roll back. Only stock transfers set a timeout.
findings.recommendation: Set { timeout, maxWait } on posting transactions and batch-insert voucher lines and movements.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a shared POSTING_TRANSACTION_OPTIONS = { timeout: 30000, maxWait: 10000 } and pass it to every posting $transaction. Replace per-line voucher_line inserts with createMany or a single multi-row INSERT.

findings.description: Sale posting locks stock balance rows in invoice line order while transfers lock by id; two concurrent sales with the same items in different order can deadlock.
findings.evidence: for (const line of lines) { SELECT ... FOR UPDATE }
findings.recommendation: Lock balance rows in a deterministic order (sorted by item id, holder id) in every posting service.
findings.fixPrompt: In sale-post.service.ts and the other post services, sort the lines by item_id before acquiring FOR UPDATE locks on inventory_stock_balances.

findings.description: Critical ERP paths are untested. backend/test has 3 Vitest files (~350 lines: account codes, balance helper, password hashing, access rules, stock holders), all untracked. No tests for any *-post.service.ts, reversal/void, fiscal close, opening balances, stock movement/balance consistency, reports, or auth routes. Frontend has 0 tests while jest.config sets 50-90% coverage thresholds.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests against a real Postgres (Testcontainers or CI service): post/reverse each document type, GL vs stock reconciliation, fiscal close and next-year Balance Sheet, opening balances, 401/403 per role.
findings.fixPrompt: Set up a Vitest integration suite that starts Postgres (Testcontainers), runs prisma migrate deploy, seeds a company, and tests: purchase post (GL inventory = stock value), sale post (COGS from locked average), void rejection for posted vouchers, year close then Balance Sheet difference = 0, trial balance with mid-year opening balance, and role-based 403s.

findings.description: CI exists but is untracked and incomplete: triggers on 'develop' while the remote uses 'dev'; no lint, no prisma validate / migrate diff, no frontend tests, no dependency audit, no Docker build, no CD.
findings.recommendation: Commit the workflow, fix branch names, add lint, prisma validate + migrate diff, npm audit --omit=dev, Docker build, and frontend tests.
findings.fixPrompt: Edit .github/workflows/ci.yml: branches [main, dev]; add jobs for npm run lint (both apps), npx prisma validate and migrate diff --exit-code, npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev, docker build for both Dockerfiles, and frontend jest.

findings.description: Unused frontend dependencies remain (never imported): ag-grid-community, ag-grid-react, exceljs, @auth/core, query-string, clsx, dotenv, @next/env, @mantine/hooks, supertest, playwright (no e2e), @types/express, tsx. puppeteer, bullmq, redis, pg and aws-sdk were removed since the last audit.
findings.recommendation: Remove unused packages (keep exceljs only if Excel export is built for DATA-018/UIUX export).
findings.fixPrompt: In frontend/package.json remove ag-grid-community, ag-grid-react, @auth/core, query-string, dotenv, @next/env, supertest, @types/express, tsx and playwright if no e2e tests are planned; verify with npm run type-check and npm run build.

findings.description: Peer-dependency conflicts are hidden with --legacy-peer-deps: @typescript-eslint 7.18 requires eslint ^8.56 but eslint 9.39 is installed; @testing-library/react 14.3 requires React 18 but React 19.2 is installed. CI runs npm ci without the flag and will likely fail with ERESOLVE.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to typescript-eslint v8 and @testing-library/react v16, then drop --legacy-peer-deps.
findings.fixPrompt: In frontend upgrade @typescript-eslint/* to v8 and @testing-library/react to v16, remove --legacy-peer-deps from the Dockerfile, run npm ci, lint and type-check.

findings.description: Node versions differ: frontend engines/.nvmrc/Dockerfile use 24, backend Dockerfile and CI use 22.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on one LTS (Node 24) across Dockerfiles, CI, engines and .nvmrc.
findings.fixPrompt: Set Node 24 in backend/Dockerfile, .github/workflows/ci.yml and add a root .nvmrc; add engines to backend/package.json.

findings.description: Containers now run as non-root and Next.js has output: 'standalone', but the frontend Dockerfile still installs full production node_modules, copies .next and runs npm start, so the standalone build is unused and the image is larger than needed.
findings.recommendation: Copy .next/standalone and .next/static and run node server.js.
findings.fixPrompt: Rewrite the frontend Dockerfile runner stage to COPY .next/standalone, .next/static and public, then CMD ["node","server.js"]; drop the second npm ci.

findings.description: Logs are plain-text morgan access logs with no request ids; the Next proxy forwards only accept, content-type and x-company-id, so the backend sees the frontend container IP for every user (breaks IP throttling and audit).
findings.recommendation: Generate/forward x-request-id and x-forwarded-for, set trust proxy, log JSON.
findings.fixPrompt: In the Next proxy route forward x-forwarded-for and an x-request-id (crypto.randomUUID when absent). In app.ts set trust proxy and replace morgan with pino-http using the request id.

findings.description: deployment/ is partly copied from another project: OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL, FRONTEND_URL '*', UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR, SUPPORTED_LOCALES and an uploads volume are unused; DEFAULT_COMPANY_ID is hardcoded; CORS_ORIGIN is not set; env examples still contain placeholder secrets with no startup rejection.
findings.recommendation: Trim to the variables the code reads, set CORS_ORIGIN, remove DEFAULT_COMPANY_ID, and reject placeholder secrets at startup.
findings.fixPrompt: Edit deployment/docker-compose.yml to keep only variables read by backend/src/config/env.ts; add CORS_ORIGIN; remove DEFAULT_COMPANY_ID and OPENAI/upload settings. In env.ts reject secrets that start with 'your_' or are shorter than 32 characters in production.

findings.description: The frontend image healthcheck calls GET /, which the auth middleware redirects (307) to /login, so the check always fails in the root compose (deployment/ overrides it).
findings.recommendation: Point the healthcheck at /login or a dedicated /api/health route excluded from the middleware matcher.
findings.fixPrompt: Add frontend/src/app/api/health/route.ts returning 200, exclude it in the middleware matcher, and use it in the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK.

findings.description: Graceful shutdown has no timeout (keep-alive connections can block it) and compose healthchecks use liveness /health instead of /health/database for readiness.
findings.recommendation: Add a forced-exit timeout and prisma.$disconnect on shutdown; use /health/database for readiness.
findings.fixPrompt: In server.ts add a 10s forced exit timer after SIGTERM, call prisma.$disconnect(), and change the backend compose healthcheck to /api/v1/health/database.

findings.description: Setup and deployment docs describe a different architecture (Redis, MinIO, BullMQ worker, TypeORM, tRPC) and point to the broken root compose; none cover migrations, admin seeding, backups or the deployment/ folder. There is no end-user guide for accountants or storekeepers.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite README/SETUP for the real stack and add a DEPLOYMENT.md runbook plus a short user guide per module.
findings.fixPrompt: Rewrite README.md and frontend/SETUP.md to describe Next.js + Express + Prisma + PostgreSQL only; add DEPLOYMENT.md covering env vars, migrate deploy, seed:admin, backup/restore, rollback and TLS.

findings.description: Account ranges, classes and dates are hardcoded in feature code, against project rules: Balance Sheet / P&L classify by code prefix ('01'–'05'), voucher cash/bank detection uses fixed prefixes, the trial balance invents '3999999999', reports fall back to `${year}-01-01` (breaks non-calendar fiscal years), and the frontend still falls back to a fixed company UUID.
findings.recommendation: Classify by accountType / normalBalance from the chart of accounts, read cash/bank accounts from bank-account and settings tables, default dates from the active fiscal year, and remove the fixed company UUID fallback.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace code-prefix classification in balance-sheet and profit-and-loss services with account.accountType. Replace cashAccountCodePrefixes in voucher.service.ts with a lookup of accounts linked to bank accounts or flagged as cash. Default report dates from the active fiscal year endpoint. Remove the default company UUID in backend-client.ts.

findings.description: Type-safety escapes are concentrated in finance code: 13 `any` uses including voucher mappers and a transaction typed as any in bank cheques.
findings.recommendation: Type mappers with Prisma.VoucherGetPayload and transactions with Prisma.TransactionClient.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace `any` in voucher.service.ts mappers with Prisma.VoucherGetPayload<{ include: { lines: true } }> and in bank-cheque.service.ts with Prisma.TransactionClient. Run npm run type-check.

findings.description: Every route handler repeats the same try { resolveAccessScope … new XService(companyId, scope) … } catch(next) boilerplate.
findings.evidence: try { const scope = await resolveAccessScope(req); const service = new ProductService(...); ... } catch (e) { next(e) }
findings.recommendation: Add an asyncHandler and a scoped-service factory helper.
findings.fixPrompt: Create backend/src/http/handler.ts with asyncHandler(fn) and withScope(ServiceClass) helpers and refactor products.routes.ts as the pattern; then apply to other route files.

findings.description: The frontend API client still falls back to a fixed company UUID (not exploitable — the backend verifies access — but against project rules).
findings.recommendation: Remove the fallback; require an active company from the session.
findings.fixPrompt: In frontend/src/lib/api/backend-client.ts remove the hardcoded company UUID fallback and omit x-company-id when no company is selected.

findings.description: The frontend /api/v1 proxy forwards path segments with encodeURIComponent, which leaves '..' unchanged; today this only reaches the public /health endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Reject '.' and '..' segments.
findings.fixPrompt: In frontend/src/app/api/v1/[...path]/route.ts return 400 when any path segment is '.' or '..'.

findings.description: The 12 document screens users spend most time on (Purchase, Sale, both Returns, Journal, Cash/Bank and Bank Receipt vouchers and their posted lists) bypass the Calm Ledger design system: bespoke <main style={{padding:10}}> layouts, inline-style tables and two parallel table-style factories (1,079 inline style={{ in the app). Purchase/Sales use PurchaseToolbar, vouchers use VoucherPageHeader, and the newer Stock Transfer/Adjustment screens use PageHeader + .page-shell — three different patterns, and the newest modules follow DESIGN.md better than the 'Purchase pattern' AGENTS.md tells new modules to copy.
findings.evidence: <main style={{ padding: 10, ... }}>   // vs PageHeader + .page-shell in StockTransferPage
findings.recommendation: Build one shared DocumentPage + LinesPanel + DocumentSummary from components/ui and migrate the 12 screens using DESIGN.md's checklist; update AGENTS.md so the reference pattern is the one that matches DESIGN.md.
findings.fixPrompt: Create frontend/src/components/ui/DocumentPage.tsx (PageHeader with actions on top, .page-shell, header form using .form-grid, lines panel using data-table, summary area). Migrate PurchaseVoucherPage first, removing PurchaseVoucherStyles.ts inline styles, then apply the same to Sales, Returns and Vouchers. Keep behavior identical; run type-check.

findings.description: Fixed pixel header grids clip at the 1280px desktop target: with Location shown, the purchase header needs ≈1,077px but the parent card has overflow:hidden and ≈992px is available with the sidebar open, so the right-most fields are cut off. Same inline gridTemplateColumns pattern in all voucher headers.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared .form-grid with --form-cols (collapses at 900px); no inline gridTemplateColumns.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace the inline gridTemplateColumns in PurchaseHeaderForm.tsx and the voucher header grids with className="form-grid" and style={{ '--form-cols': 4 }}; remove overflow:hidden from the workspace card.

findings.description: No keyboard line entry on any voucher: no Enter-to-add-line, no Enter-to-next-field, no Save/Process shortcut. The only onKeyDown handlers are in SearchableSelect, Tabs, ConfirmDialog and search boxes. Heavy data entry is mouse-driven.
findings.recommendation: Enter on the last line field adds/updates the line and returns focus to Item; Ctrl/Cmd+S saves draft; Alt+N adds a line. Show shortcuts in button tooltips.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a useLineEntryKeyboard hook in frontend/src/components/shared/ that handles Enter (add line, focus first field), Ctrl/Cmd+S (save draft) and Alt+N (new line). Wire it into PurchaseLineEntry and every *LineTable component.

findings.description: Shared fields now wrap inputs in <label>, but 15 raw line-item inputs and the line-item SearchableSelect have no accessible name.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label combining the column and line number (e.g. 'Debit, Line 3') and pass ariaLabel to SearchableSelect.
findings.fixPrompt: In the voucher line-table components add aria-label={`${columnTitle}, Line ${index + 1}`} to every raw input and ariaLabel to SearchableSelect.

findings.description: Required, error and hint states are not exposed to assistive technology: the * is aria-hidden and inputs never get required/aria-required; aria-invalid/aria-describedby appear only twice in the codebase; hint text is not linked.
findings.recommendation: Pass required/aria-required through, link hint and error via useId + aria-describedby, add an error prop setting aria-invalid.
findings.fixPrompt: In FieldLabel.tsx and FormFields.tsx add required → aria-required, an error prop rendering a message with an id and setting aria-invalid, and aria-describedby linking hint and error ids (useId).

findings.description: Purchase/Sales/Returns message banner has no role, so success and error messages are not announced; errors show an invoice icon instead of an error icon.
findings.recommendation: Replace with the shared InlineAlert, as VoucherMessageBanner already does.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace PurchaseMessageBanner's div with InlineAlert (role=alert for errors, role=status for success) and use the danger icon for errors.

findings.description: Load failures render as friendly empty states ('No Units Yet — Add your first Unit') because pages read only { data = [], isLoading }.
findings.recommendation: Handle isError with a danger TableMessageRow and a Retry button.
findings.fixPrompt: In UomPage, CategoriesPage, ChequeBooksTab and ProductDetailPanel read isError and refetch; render <TableMessageRow tone="danger"> with a Retry button when isError.

findings.description: Approve Voucher posts to the ledger with no confirmation. In Journal Voucher the review-before-post dialog is dead code (reviewVoucher never called) and Process posts directly.
findings.recommendation: Add a ConfirmDialog for Approve and Process (show totals and posting date); wire or delete the JV review dialog.
findings.fixPrompt: In ApprovalQueuePage.tsx wrap approve in ConfirmDialog showing voucher number, date and total. In JournalVoucherPage.tsx call reviewVoucher before saveVoucher(true), or remove the unused review dialog code.

findings.description: Some numbers, dates and currency ignore settings: toLocaleString() on the dashboard, toLocaleDateString('en-US') in analytics, hardcoded currency_code 'PKR' defaults on Bank, Customers and Suppliers.
findings.recommendation: Use the settings-driven formatCount/formatDate/formatMoney helpers and default currency from general settings.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace toLocaleString/toLocaleDateString calls listed with the shared formatting helpers that read general_settings, and replace hardcoded 'PKR' defaults with the company base currency from settings.

findings.description: Icon-only buttons without accessible names in posted-document views (close button has neither aria-label nor title; others rely on title only), and one 11px font below the 12px floor.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared Button with aria-label and title; use --font-size-2xs.
findings.fixPrompt: Add aria-label to every icon-only button in Posted*View components and replace fontSize '11px' with var(--font-size-2xs).

findings.description: Large lists cannot be sorted: only ProductList uses th-sort/aria-sort; Vouchers, Customers, Suppliers and posted document lists have no sorting.
findings.recommendation: Add server-side sort on date, number and amount columns using the .th-sort pattern.
findings.fixPrompt: Add sortBy/sortDir query params to the voucher, customer, supplier and posted-document list endpoints (allowlisted enums) and .th-sort headers with aria-sort in the matching tables.

findings.description: Contrast mostly fixed (muted text 6.2:1). Remaining: --color-text-light #6b7787 is 4.21:1 on the page background; dark-theme primary/danger gradient top stops give 3.81:1 and 3.69:1 for white 13px labels.
findings.recommendation: Darken the dark-theme top stops to ≥ #3b6fe0 and restrict text-light to icons.
findings.fixPrompt: In design-tokens.css set the dark primary gradient top stop to #3b6fe0, the danger top stop to a value giving ≥4.5:1 with white, and darken --color-text-light to reach 4.5:1 on --color-bg.

findings.description: Most data tables show skeleton rows, but the 5 posted-document lists still show a text-only loading row and ui/TableSkeleton.tsx is never imported.
findings.recommendation: Use TableMessageRow loading (or TableSkeleton) in posted lists; delete TableSkeleton if unused.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace the text loading rows in Posted*View components with <TableMessageRow loading colSpan={n} />.

findings.description: No print, PDF, Excel or CSV export on any financial report. Printing exists only for purchase and sales vouchers. Accountants cannot file, send or audit a Trial Balance, Ledger, P&L or Balance Sheet.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared report print layout (company header, period, print date, user, page numbers) and CSV/Excel export for every report.
findings.fixPrompt: Create frontend/src/components/reports/ReportPrintLayout.tsx with company name, report title, period, generated-by and page footer, and a useReportExport hook producing CSV (and XLSX via exceljs). Add Print and Export buttons to the Trial Balance, Ledger, P&L, Balance Sheet and summary reports.

findings.description: Ledger Report account picker loads only the first 200 posting accounts and filters on the client. Every customer and supplier has its own linked account, so most accounts become unselectable after a few hundred parties.
findings.recommendation: Use server-side search in the picker.
findings.fixPrompt: In LedgerReportPage.tsx replace the 200-row preload with a SearchableSelect that queries /accounts?search=...&is_posting=true&limit=20 as the user types (debounced).

findings.description: Purchase/Sales/Returns summary reports total only the current page (50 rows) — footer reads 'Totals For This Page' — with no grand total, and sum with Number().
findings.evidence: rows.reduce((s, r) => s + Number(r.net_amount), 0)   // 'Totals For This Page'
findings.recommendation: Return grand totals from the backend (Decimal) with the paged rows and show both page and report totals.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a totals object (computed with SUM in SQL over the full filter) to the summary report endpoints and render it as the table footer in ReportsWorkspace.tsx.

findings.description: No drill-down: the Ledger returns voucher_id but shows the number as plain text; Trial Balance, Balance Sheet and P&L lines do not open the account ledger.
findings.recommendation: Link voucher numbers to the voucher view and account rows to the Ledger Report with the same dates.
findings.fixPrompt: In LedgerReportTable.tsx render voucher_number as a Link to the voucher detail. In the trial balance, P&L and balance sheet tables link each account row to /reports/ledger?accountId=..&dateFrom=..&dateTo=..

findings.description: The dashboard shows counts only (accounts, vouchers) plus 'sum of total_debit by month' across all voucher types, labelled like revenue. No revenue, gross margin, receivables, payables, cash/bank or stock value KPIs for management.
findings.evidence: SUM(total_debit) GROUP BY month   -- all voucher types
findings.recommendation: Derive KPIs from ledger balances by account type (Revenue, COGS, Gross Margin %, Receivables, Payables, Cash & Bank) and stock value from balances, with period comparison.
findings.fixPrompt: In dashboard.service.ts add KPIs computed from posted voucher_lines grouped by account type for the current fiscal period and the prior period, plus Σ total_stock_value. Render as KPI tiles with change vs prior period on the dashboard page.

findings.description: Report default 'today' uses the UTC date, so between midnight and 05:00 Pakistan time reports default to yesterday.
findings.recommendation: Compute today in the settings time zone.
findings.fixPrompt: Replace toISOString().slice(0,10) in LedgerReportHelpers.ts with a todayInTimeZone(settings.timeZone) helper in lib/date.ts.

findings.description: ESLint reports 22 warnings (14 exhaustive-deps, down from 28). Because the lint script uses --max-warnings 0, `npm run lint` fails, so lint cannot be a CI gate.
findings.evidence: React Hook useEffect has a missing dependency ...
findings.recommendation: Fix the 14 dependency arrays (useCallback/useMemo where needed) and the remaining warnings so lint passes.
findings.fixPrompt: Run npm run lint in frontend and fix every react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning by adding dependencies or memoizing callbacks; do not add eslint-disable comments.

findings.description: Frontend type safety is switched off: @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any is 'off' and 208 `any` remain, concentrated in API clients and settings props.
findings.recommendation: Set the rule to warn and type the API clients first.
